body.x: LBS Tech Co., Ltd. (CEO Siwan Lee) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, to be held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9, as part of the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion.

LBS Tech is a spatial information specialist company that has focused on solving mobility rights and accessibility issues for people with limited mobility through pedestrian-based spatial information technologies. Starting with pedestrian information services for people with visual impairments and wheelchair users, LBS Tech has expanded into future mobility areas, including autonomous driving, delivery robots, and smart cities, leveraging years of expertise in collecting, classifying, and processing pedestrian pathway data.

In particular, LBS Tech defines “pedestrian pathways” as a core data asset that existing map and navigation technologies have not sufficiently addressed. The company precisely collects elements that directly affect real-world movement, such as pathway width, slope, surface condition, level differences, and obstacles. It processes them by disability type and user characteristics to provide customized mobility routes. Through this approach, it has realized “door-to-door” mobility, connecting movement from vehicle drop-off points to destination entrances.

Since winning the Best Mobile Use Case Award for accessibility and inclusivity at MWC Barcelona 2023, LBS Tech has demonstrated its technological strength and innovation by receiving the CES 2025 Innovation Award in the Human Security category and the Best of Innovation Award in the Travel & Tourism category at CES 2026.

In Korea, LBS Tech has carried out pedestrian pathway data collection and processing projects in cooperation with organizations such as the Korea Labor Force Development Institute for the Aged and the Korea Employment Agency for Persons with Disabilities. It has also implemented smart city projects that utilize pedestrian pathway data in locations such as Sejong Smart City and Busan Eco Delta City.

Overseas, starting with an AR-based mobile pedestrian navigation pilot project conducted in the Barking and Dagenham area of London in 2024, LBS Tech collaborated with the West Midlands Combined Authority (WMCA) in 2025 to demonstrate AR pedestrian mobility and tourism information services for people with limited mobility in the Birmingham area. The company is currently planning further collaboration with Aston University to develop an integrated pedestrian environment system linked with autonomous driving technologies.

At this exhibition, LBS Tech will present ‘MaaS-Bridge,’ a core technology that received the Best of Innovation Award in the CES 2026 Travel & Tourism category. MaaS-Bridge is a new concept mobility connectivity system designed for the autonomous driving era. While existing MaaS (Mobility as a Service) focuses on vehicle-centered integrated mobility services, MaaS-Bridge addresses the disconnection between vehicles and pedestrian pathways.

As autonomous driving technologies become more widespread, the importance of the segment from vehicle drop-off to the final destination continues to grow compared with vehicle movement itself. For people with visual impairments, wheelchair users, and older adults, usable pedestrian environments vary even when the destination is the same. LBS Tech, therefore, focused on the idea that the closest drop-off point is not always the optimal choice.

MaaS-Bridge comprehensively analyzes road traffic flow, the condition of pedestrian pathways near destinations, and user mobility characteristics to design optimal pick-up and drop-off points tailored to each user type. LBS Tech defines these as “Mobility Points (MP),” enabling users to continue safely and accessibly to their destinations via suitable pedestrian pathways even after leaving the vehicle.

The core value of this technology lies in expanding the activity range of people with limited mobility beyond everyday urban travel to include leisure and tourism. By designing an uninterrupted experience that spans the entire journey from beginning to end, MaaS-Bridge is recognized as a new standard for inclusive mobility.

LBS Tech has carried out data construction and sales projects in the Asian region and, recently, has exported spatial information–based datasets to the United Kingdom through linkage with pilot projects.

In the future, the company aims to enter the North American and European markets, where awareness of universal mobility rights is high and autonomous driving technologies are under active development.

An LBS Tech official said, “Our goal is to conduct proof-of-concept projects with global companies connected through CES. Through this, we aim to demonstrate the practical importance of pedestrian technologies in the final stage of autonomous driving. If this verification is achieved, we expect collaboration opportunities to expand naturally thereafter.”

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
